column1: # replay-lanes.tsv -- how the demo recorder's unit codec cuts a unit image into lanes, and which
# of them its rules predict (tagpu_recfmt.h, the unit frame). tools/replay-lanes-gen.py says what
# the columns and roles mean and generates inc/tagpu_reclanes.h from this file; the build fails
# when the two disagree. Each recording carries the table it was written with (RT_CODEC), so a
# change here never orphans a recording.
# The widths are the record's own field boundaries where they are not dwords: research/sizelab/
# units/frame.py lanes_field(), the size round's lane study, with the mover's +0x26 and +0x28
# words joined into the claim stamp's dword. A width is a size hint, never a correctness one: a
# wrong boundary costs bytes and loses none. The roles name the fields a rule of the unit frame
# computes; each such row cites the rule's engine fact. "(map)" is the engine map's *The unit and
# player records, byte by byte* (research/notes/exe-reverse-engineering.md), where every field's
